concept: A cohort groups entities by a shared starting period, such as their first order month. Cohort analysis measures behavior as time passes after that starting point.
example:
WITH FirstOrder AS (
    SELECT CustomerID, MIN(OrderDate) AS FirstOrderDate
    FROM Orders GROUP BY CustomerID
)
SELECT DATEFROMPARTS(YEAR(FirstOrderDate), MONTH(FirstOrderDate), 1) AS CohortMonth,
       COUNT(*) AS Customers
FROM FirstOrder
GROUP BY DATEFROMPARTS(YEAR(FirstOrderDate), MONTH(FirstOrderDate), 1);
breakdown: MIN finds the first observed order for each customer.
DATEFROMPARTS normalizes the date to the first of the month.
Grouping on CohortMonth counts customers who started in each month.
A full retention table additionally needs activity months and months-since-cohort.
practice: Return each customer and their first-order cohort month without aggregating the customers together.
answer:
SELECT CustomerID,
       DATEFROMPARTS(YEAR(MIN(OrderDate)), MONTH(MIN(OrderDate)), 1) AS CohortMonth
FROM Orders
GROUP BY CustomerID;
takeaways: Define cohort entry precisely; first observed order may not be first-ever order.
Retention needs a clear activity definition and denominator.

deep_dive.heading: Building cohorts without look-ahead bias
paragraphs: A cohort is defined by an entry event such as first purchase, not by the date of any later transaction. Derive each customer's first observed event, then compute month offsets for subsequent activity.
Retention denominators should be the number of customers in the original cohort, not the number active in a later month. Explicitly define whether month zero counts as retained.
Partial recent months can make retention appear worse. Compare only cohorts with complete observation windows or label the censoring.
questions: How would you calculate retention percentages from this output?
Why can incomplete observation windows distort the latest cohorts?
deep_dive.code:
WITH FirstOrder AS (
    SELECT CustomerID, MIN(OrderDate) AS FirstOrderDate
    FROM Orders GROUP BY CustomerID
), Activity AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT o.CustomerID,
           DATEFROMPARTS(YEAR(f.FirstOrderDate), MONTH(f.FirstOrderDate), 1) AS CohortMonth,
           DATEDIFF(MONTH, DATEFROMPARTS(YEAR(f.FirstOrderDate), MONTH(f.FirstOrderDate), 1), DATEFROMPARTS(YEAR(o.OrderDate), MONTH(o.OrderDate), 1)) AS MonthNumber
    FROM Orders AS o JOIN FirstOrder AS f ON o.CustomerID = f.CustomerID
)
SELECT CohortMonth, MonthNumber, COUNT(*) AS ActiveCustomers
FROM Activity GROUP BY CohortMonth, MonthNumber;
